column6: Advocated sustainable community grants, programs for women- and minority-owned businesses, incentives for young entrepreneurs, business incubators, and cultural centers in an August 1, 2024 interview.
As a Hartnell College trustee, moved to adopt a resolution affirming the college's commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion. It passed.

As a member of the Higher Education Budget Subcommittee, sent the University of Florida a 21-question oversight letter. It concerned the university's public condemnation of diversity, equity, and inclusion programs. It also asked about its institutional-neutrality policy.

As Pembroke Select Board chair, led the board's 2021 interviews of applicants for the town's new Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee. She asked applicants whether they had signed a petition to disband the committee.

As president of AAUW of Idaho, wrote a guest opinion criticizing the State Board of Education's ban on diversity, equity and inclusion programs at public colleges. She also objected to the closing of campus women's centers.
As Reynoldsburg council president pro tempore, Baker signed an ordinance sharing the city's diversity, equality, and inclusion officer with the school district.
Asked Greensboro City Council to keep funding its minority- and women-owned business program while considering a disparity study.
Authored AB 766 requiring state agencies under the Governor to write and report diversity, equity, and inclusion plans. It passed the Assembly 60-18, but the Governor vetoed it on October 13, 2025.
Cast the sole no vote against reappointing Theresa Devine to the Ellensburg Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Commission; the reappointment carried 6-1.
Championed creation of Smithfield's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Task Force after racist graffiti was reported in town; the council approved its founding resolution.
Chris Mathis publicly opposed Arizona SB1694's restrictions on public-sector diversity programs, describing the measure as viewpoint discrimination.
Co-offered Boston’s ordinance creating a supplier-diversity program and reporting requirements to increase meaningful participation by minority- and women-owned businesses in city contracts.
Co-sponsored a college overhaul that became law, barring race- or sex-based preferences and diversity, equity, and inclusion offices at Arkansas public universities (House Bill 1512, Act 341).

Co-sponsored a Jefferson City Council bill to remove diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) policies from city boards, departments, and commissions; the City Council defeated the bill.

Co-sponsored a Tennessee law requiring the head of each public college or university to certify yearly that the school used no preference favoring a group to increase diversity, equity, or inclusion. The certifications go to the state comptroller of the treasury, the state's financial watchdog, starting January 1, 2027, and the law lets the attorney general investigate. It took effect May 22, 2026 (Senate Bill 1713).

Co-sponsored Senate Bill 26. The proposal bars Kentucky school districts and the state education department from spending on diversity, equity, and inclusion programs, and closes the department's diversity division.

Co-sponsored the Arkansas ACCESS Act, a higher-education law barring public colleges from requiring diversity statements and changing scholarship, concurrent-credit, and accelerated-course rules (House Bill 1512, Act 341 of 2025).

Cosponsored HB 1788 in 2026 to void contracts containing DEI provisions and allow taxpayer lawsuits over public entities’ contracts with such provisions. The Senate referred it for interim study on April 16, 2026.
During the 2025 Wyoming General Session, the Honor Wyoming legislative scorecard reports that Stacy Jones voted yes on SF 103, Terminating and defunding diversity, equity and inclusion.
Introduced a bill on February 26, 2025 to raise the share of state contracts set aside for minority- and women-owned businesses from 15 to 20 percent. It did not pass.
Introduced a bill with Rep. Anna Paulina Luna to ban race-based preferences and quotas in federal contracting.
Introduced the Diversity, Equity, Inclusion Dead on Arrival Act.
Issued a formal legal opinion that employer diversity, equity, and inclusion programs are legal under federal law.

Issued a legal opinion asserting that roughly 80 Florida laws and programs supporting minority contracting and diverse appointments violated equal-protection guarantees, and said his office would no longer enforce or defend those provisions.
Johnson sponsored enacted SB 1083 and SB 1084, known as the Dismantle DEI in Employment Act and Dismantling DEI Departments Act.

Johnson sponsored enacted SB 1713 requiring annual attestations that public higher-education institutions have not implemented discriminatory preferences to increase diversity, equity, or inclusion and authorizing related attorney-general investigations.

Joined a congressional brief opposing race-based college admissions in the Harvard and UNC cases. It argued that the policies discriminated and violated equal-treatment protections (Students for Fair Admissions).

Joined a May 9, 2022 Supreme Court brief opposing race-conscious admissions at Harvard and the University of North Carolina. It sought reversal and overruling of Grutter under equal-protection and federal funding laws. It preserved a limited exception for remedying an institution's own past discrimination.

Joined the congressional amicus brief in the consolidated Harvard and UNC admissions cases arguing that race-conscious admissions violated equal protection and Title VI and urging the Supreme Court to overrule Grutter.
Joined the No Kings protest at the Michigan Capitol and opposed the Trump administration's restrictions on diversity, equity, and inclusion programs.
Led a protest outside the U.S. Supreme Court in support of affirmative action during arguments in Schuette v. Coalition to Defend Affirmative Action.
Made the motion to adopt San Mateo's first citywide diversity, equity and inclusion plan for city operations; it passed 4-0.
Made the motion to keep the city's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion manager job. It failed 2-3.
Made the motion to name affirmative action officers and require yearly equity training for all school staff. The board approved it 6-2.
Made the motion to suspend the school division's diversity, equity, and inclusion policy. It passed 4-3.
Met his state representative as a constituent to argue against Alabama's anti-DEI law, which limits diversity, equity, and inclusion programs (Senate Bill 129).
Moved and voted to extend the district’s remedial program for minority- and women-owned business participation in construction, goods, and services.
Moved to approve an agreement with Corwin for access, diversity, equity and inclusion services and products; the Governing Board approved it 3-0 on September 5, 2023.
Moved to approve two contracts totaling $74,770 for diversity, equity, and inclusion training for city staff. The council approved them with no votes against.

On 2024-06-26, voted to let large public-works bids be scored for participation by certified disadvantaged businesses, including minority-, women- and veteran-owned firms. The House passed the bill 39–0, and it became law.
On 2025-01-13, Aleks Vranicic addressed the Mesa City Council and requested review of its diversity, equity and inclusion policy while suggesting merit-based decisions.
On 2025-02-03, Aleks Vranicic addressed the Mesa City Council and requested that it reconsider and remove its diversity, equity and inclusion policy.
On 2025-02-25, Josie Barnhart voted with the New Hanover County Board of Education majority to remove diversity, equity, and inclusion references from district policy; the vote was 5-2.

On April 4, 2025, Representative Michelle McCane publicly condemned a U.S. Department of Education threat to withhold school funding unless schools certified bans on diversity, equity, and inclusion programs.

On the Solano Community College board, seconded and voted for a resolution backing Proposition 16, which sought to end California's ban on affirmative action. The same night, she voted for a resolution backing Proposition 15, higher property taxes on large commercial property to fund schools and local services. Both passed unanimously.
Opposed Senate Bill 474 and defended diversity, equity, and inclusion, urging lawmakers not to support legislation driven by political hostility to DEI.
Publicly defended the military's diversity, equity and inclusion programs in a July 2023 interview, calling Republican attacks on them "a bunch of hooey."
Seconded and voted for creating a school district inclusion and diversity officer job, which passed 5-2. He also moved a $100 bonus for staff who got a COVID-19 booster; it passed 4-3.
Served as co-chair of the Minnesota Supreme Court Committee for Equality and Justice and led development of a judiciary diversity, equity, and inclusion training requirement.
Signed Senate Bill 17 in June 2023, banning diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) offices and programs at Texas public colleges and universities.

Sponsored a bill proposing to withhold state money from Arizona public colleges and universities that offer diversity, equity, and inclusion courses. Governor Katie Hobbs vetoed it on May 5, 2025 (Senate Bill 1694).
Sponsored a bill that barred waiving the state's minority business contracting rules, even during a declared emergency. It passed the House 60-9 on July 1, 2021.
Sponsored a law requiring the state to give contractors a list of certified minority- and women-owned businesses. It also makes the state publish every waiver of those hiring goals.
Sponsored a law, signed on June 24, 2024, that lets the state's chief purchasing officer waive contractor bond rules for certified minority- and women-owned businesses on public works jobs.
Sponsored a law, signed on June 24, 2025, that requires the state to give every bidder on a construction project a list of certified minority- and women-owned businesses.
Sponsored a law, signed on June 27, 2022, that requires the state diversity office to create yearly cultural competency training for all state and city workers.
Sponsored Arizona House Concurrent Resolution 2042, which passed the House and proposed prohibitions on preferential treatment and discrimination based on race or ethnicity.
Sponsored Maryland SB 829, extending and adding reports for the Minority Business Enterprise Program; the governor approved it as Chapter 621 on May 20, 2025.
Sponsored Senate File 0103, titled Terminating and defunding diversity, equity and inclusion.
Submitted Phoenix budget comments supporting a diversity, equity and inclusion office and unarmed responders for noncriminal calls.
Submitted testimony to the Defense Advisory Committee on Diversity and Inclusion opposing critical-race-theory and diversity, equity, and inclusion policies in the military.

Testified for AAUW of Idaho against a bill banning diversity, equity and inclusion offices, diversity training and bias reporting systems at Idaho's public colleges (Senate Bill 1198). She opposed it in Senate and House committees; it became law in April 2025.
Voted against HB 2460, which restricted diversity, equity, and inclusion practices at public universities.

Voted against House passage of SB129, the 2024 bill barring public universities and agencies from maintaining diversity, equity and inclusion offices and from teaching listed divisive concepts, which became Act 2024-34; the House vote was 75-28.
Voted against keeping the city's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion manager job. The motion to keep it failed 2-3.

Voted against passing S.B. 1, the Advance Ohio Higher Education Act, which banned diversity offices at public universities and barred faculty strikes. It passed the Ohio House 59-34 and was signed into law.
Voted against suspending the school division's diversity, equity, and inclusion policy. The suspension passed 4-3.
Voted for a council resolution reaffirming Lewiston's commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion; it passed unanimously.
Voted for a higher education overhaul that ended diversity programs at public colleges, barred faculty strikes, and added performance reviews for tenured faculty (Senate Bill 1).
Voted for ACA 5, proposing repeal of the state constitutional ban on race- and sex-conscious affirmative action in public education, employment and contracting. It passed the Assembly 60–14.
Voted for BART Resolution 5446 supporting repeal of Proposition 209 and restoration of affirmative action in California; the board adopted the resolution unanimously.
Voted for HB2105 (81-40), restricting diversity, equity, and inclusion practices at public colleges.
